message:
test(build): present is not committed, and the check could not tell

Test 1.

7cbcd0a read the disk. A file sitting untracked in a working directory passed it and failed for
everybody else -- which is the exact defect it was written to prevent. The guard had the same blind
spot as the mistake.

So it asks git what is tracked and compares. Registering a source that exists but is not committed
now fails by name: "on disk but not committed: src/untracked_probe.cpp". 521 entries checked
against 377 tracked paths today.

When git cannot be reached it SKIPS and says so rather than passing. A lookup that quietly answers
"nothing untracked" because it found nothing at all is the failure mode this file exists to catch,
and it would have been the fourth time in this task that a scan reported a clean bill by finding
nothing.

I found this by making the same error one level up. I told the reviewer three times that HEAD
configured cleanly, having measured it against my own working tree -- which is not a clean
checkout, and where the file in question was sitting. A pristine `git archive HEAD` export does
fail, though for an unrelated reason: the WebView2 SDK is a fetched prerequisite and the installer
payload references remote60_client_shell unconditionally, so a tree without it dies at generate.
Zero "Cannot find source file" errors, which is the part that was mine and is fixed.
